clue.text: Artful trick sounds trifling

indicators.note: 'sounds' tells us to take a word as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: slight means trifling or minor; the answer is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A cunning trick that turns out, by the sound of it, to be a petty one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight, as in sleight of hand, is dexterous deception used by conjurors and cheats.

clue.text: Kind of court for a bounder?

blocks.note: first meaning: an irregular, self-appointed tribunal
second meaning, read literally: an animal that moves by bounding

explanation.surface: Asking what sort of tribunal would try a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is old British slang for a cad, which suggests a court for disciplining scoundrels; read literally it is a leaping Australian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock tribunal that ignores due process carries this name, and the marsupial itself travels by hopping.

clue.text: Up-to-date news of city trial

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Fresh reports about a court case in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest, as in 'have you heard the latest?', means the most recent news or developments.

clue.text: Live, suitable for crops and manageable

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
arable land can be ploughed and planted

explanation.surface: Describing farmland that is lively, good for growing and easy to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bearable can be tolerated or coped with, so it is within one's ability to handle.

clue.text: Familiar road fine for jogging

indicators.note: jogging jolts things about, so the letters before it are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-known road that is good for running along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar' looks like an adjective describing the road, but as a noun a familiar is a close companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar, used as a noun, is an intimate associate or close companion, which is what a friend is.

clue.text: Stop at university for medical exam

blocks.note: to check is to halt or stop
being up means being in residence at university, in British usage

explanation.surface: A student pauses at college to see the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain you go up to university and come down when you leave, so being 'up' means being there.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkup is a routine examination by a doctor to assess general health.

clue.text: Girl with talent, we hear, featuring in yearbook

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the words before it count only by their sound

blocks.note: Alma is a girl's name
a knack is a talent; only its sound is kept

explanation.surface: A gifted girl gets a mention in the annual school book.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual publication of calendars, tides, statistics and other facts for the coming year.

clue.text: It's quiet back round the world's homely spots

indicators.note: going back means reading the word for silence from right to left
round says those letters wrap around the following piece

blocks.note: sh! is a call for quiet
the world is the Earth

explanation.surface: Peaceful corners of the globe that feel like home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth is the fireside floor of a home, a symbol of domestic comfort, hence cosy places.

clue.text: Chose knitting with stitch as a social activity

indicators.note: knitting interweaves strands, so the letters of the words around it are woven together into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone opted for knitting circles as a way of socialising.
explanation.walkthrough: The knitting surface hides a dance: a social activity, in a loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The schottische is a German-origin round dance similar to a slow polka, performed at social gatherings.

clue.text: Run to get acceptance in Europe nowadays

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to where the money is used, standing loosely for the noun

blocks.note: in cricket a single is one run
an idea with currency is generally accepted

explanation.surface: Hurrying to win approval in present-day Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The single currency is the euro, shared by many European countries; the definition is a loose pointer to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro, a common monetary unit adopted across much of the continent, is commonly called this.

clue.text: See 10
Tea's never-ending appeal

indicators.note: never-ending means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: charm is appeal or attractiveness

explanation.surface: The endless attraction of a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is British slang for tea, from the Chinese cha.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is informal British English for tea, borrowed from the Mandarin and Hindi word cha.

clue.text: Our bard out to reform lyrical poet

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the preceding letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Our local poet is out to change his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubadours were medieval Provençal poet-musicians who composed and sang verses of courtly love.

clue.text: The last stage is the drive to the house

blocks.note: first meaning: the final part of a race or task
second meaning, read literally: a stretch of road leading to one's dwelling

explanation.surface: The final leg of a journey is the trip up the driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: The final straight of a racecourse, and by extension the closing phase of any undertaking, carries this name.

clue.text: Called for hospital department and became unwell

blocks.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat; 'for' just introduces it
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: Someone summoned to the ear, nose and throat ward then fell sick.
explanation.definitionFit: If a plan entailed something, it required or necessitated it as a consequence.

clue.text: Mathematicians study this, possibly in a body

blocks.note: first meaning: the branch of mathematics dealing with rates of change
second meaning: a stone formed in an organ such as the kidney

explanation.surface: Mathematicians perhaps studying collectively, as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a body' suggests mathematicians studying together; it really means inside a human body, where a medical stone can form.
explanation.definitionFit: Differential and integral reckoning is a maths branch; medically the same term names a hard concretion like a gallstone.

clue.text: Further improvement

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to promote or help along
second meaning: a noun, a step forward or development

explanation.walkthrough: 'Further' looks like an adjective modifying improvement, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance a cause is to promote it, and an advance is progress or a breakthrough.

clue.text: Commit prisoner to write name

blocks.note: a con is a convict
to sign is to write one's name

explanation.surface: An inmate is made to put his signature to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign is to hand over or deliver into someone's keeping, as one commits a body to the grave.

clue.text: Refer to the unusual  rise, one to make public

indicators.note: unusual means not in the normal form, so the word after it is rearranged

blocks.note: to advert to something is a formal way to refer to it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mentioning a strange increase that someone wants to announce.
explanation.walkthrough: Advert here is the rare verb meaning to turn attention to, not the British word for an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertiser is a person or firm that publicises products or announcements to the wider world.

clue.text: It's different under English weather

indicators.note: something different has been changed, so the following letters take another order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A remark that the climate is not the same beneath English skies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather' looks like a noun about climate; here it is the verb meaning to come through a hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm is to survive it, which means to last out or withstand it.

clue.text: One way to make it!

blocks.note: surface reading: a route to success, as in making it big
setter's reading: a set of instructions for preparing a dish, 'it' being the food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make it' suggests achieving success; read literally it is about cooking something.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookery formula lists ingredients and steps, which is literally a method for producing a dish.

clue.text: Money means to make a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the word travels in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a tool is a means to an end

explanation.surface: Cash is the way to return to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is informal slang for cash, originally plunder or stolen goods.

clue.text: Lessons in the catering department?

blocks.note: surface reading: classes in cookery at a college
setter's reading: a programme of study with work placements layered between terms, named after a snack food

explanation.surface: Classes taught in a college kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a degree course that alternates periods of study with periods of work in industry, like layers of filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The British term for a degree alternating academic terms with industrial placements borrows its name from a snack, matching catering.

clue.text: See 23
Colour left traces, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters are one possible rearrangement among many

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paint left marks behind, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red hue with a slight orange tinge.

clue.text: Place involved in current increase to spend money

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
a surge is a sudden rise in electric current

explanation.surface: An electrical power spike costs a location money.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend lavishly or extravagantly, often on a treat.
